 Print overflowing Anaipillayar checkdam near bodi in Theni district Madurai: Heavy rain disrupted normal life across southern Tamil Nadu on Thursday, prompting school closures in Tirunelveli, Tuticorin, Tenkasi and Kanyakumari districts. Following an orange alert, a bathing ban was imposed at Kumbakarai Falls in Theni district from Thursday afternoon. Forest officials asked visitors bathing in the falls to leave the area. Floodwater overtopped the Anaipillaiyar check dam near Bodi after heavy rain, raising concerns over sudden surges. The water level at Vaigai dam rose to 45.60 feet on Thursday from 44.88 feet on Wednesday, while Mullaperiyar dam reached 117.90 feet, up from 116.90 feet. In Tirunelveli district, Oothu, Naalumukku, Kakachi and Manjolai hamlets in the Western Ghats received good rainfall until Thursday morning, though no rain was recorded elsewhere in the district that morning. Several parts of Tenkasi district received widespread rainfall during the day. Surulacode recorded the highest rainfall in Kanyakumari district at 10.5cm as of Thursday morning. Waterlogging was reported on some roads near Nithiravilai and Derisanamcope within Nagercoil corporation limits. Heavy inflows were also reported in the Thamirabarani and Pazhayar rivers. In Tuticorin district, Tiruchendur recorded the highest rainfall at 11.76cm, while waterlogging affected a few areas within Tuticorin corporation limits. Meanwhile, Madurai district collector Nishant Krishna, chairing a monsoon preparedness meeting on Thursday, directed officials to monitor vulnerable areas where rainwater was likely to stagnate and complete precautionary works before heavy rain. He instructed officials to use high-capacity motor pumps and special vehicles to drain water immediately from low-lying areas, subways and major roads. He also called for inspections of canals and underground drainage systems to ensure unobstructed water flow and prevent blockages in rainwater drainage connections, manholes, water bodies and streams. The collector directed officials to ensure uninterrupted power supply to hospitals during the rainy season and keep generators ready with adequate fuel stocks.
